clue.text: Useless old track in Leicester

parts.note: something useless is a dud
a ley is an old track or alignment across the landscape, as in ley lines

explanation.surface: A disused old track running through the city of Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leicester' looks like the city, but it is the man: Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite, was made Earl of Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley held the title Earl of Leicester, so the earldom's name stands for the courtier.

clue.text: Relaxed, with lowered pulse

parts.note: lowered means brought down
a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: Calm, with a slowed heart rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-key and unexcited, as in a laid-back, understated mood.

clue.text: While the Light lasted, any old thing in the end got broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order
only the final letter of the word thing is used

explanation.surface: During the daylight, some random object was eventually transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got broadcast' rearranges ANY OLD into DAYLON; 'in the end' adds G, the last letter of 'thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting through the whole of the daytime, from dawn to dusk.

clue.text: Contrives a device with handles, I'm told

indicators.note: signals that the letters match what is heard rather than written

parts.note: an engine for a machine and ears for handles, ears being the handles on a jug

explanation.surface: Someone schemes up a gadget with grips, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Handles are ears, as on a jug; ENGINE plus EARS is said just like the verb meaning contrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to bring it about by skilful scheming, to arrange or plot it.

clue.text: Voyager makes room to take crew member

parts.note: room in the sense of free space
a man is a member of a crew or team

explanation.surface: A traveller makes space aboard to take on another sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels through the cosmos, so is a voyager beyond Earth.

clue.text: Dante's brothers, such admirers of fifteenth century art

definitions.meaning: Dante Gabriel Rossetti co-founded the Brotherhood of English painters in 1848
the group revered Italian painting before the time of Raphael

explanation.surface: Fellows of the Italian poet, devotees of early Renaissance painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante suggests the medieval poet, but this is Dante Gabriel Rossetti, the Victorian painter and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossetti's Victorian art movement called itself a Brotherhood and looked back to early Italian painting.

clue.text: Protection for copyright has expired

parts.note: C is the copyright symbol, a C in a circle
something that has expired is over

explanation.surface: Shielding for a copyright that has lapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelter or insurance that shields one from harm or loss.

clue.text: Two months and a half at sea

indicators.note: two signals the abbreviated month is used twice

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March

indicators.note: half of the word at, its first letter

explanation.surface: Ten weeks spent afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles MAR (March); 'half' takes the first of the two letters of 'at'. The Sea of Marmara lies between the Black Sea and the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inland body of salt water in Turkey linking the Bosporus and the Dardanelles.

clue.text: Not available to take employment — a symptom of illness

parts.note: use in the sense of employment, being put to work

explanation.surface: Being unable to take a job is a sign of sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A queasy sickly feeling is a typical sign of being unwell.

clue.text: Love or hate, say, can't be decently expressed

definitions.meaning: each is a word of four letters
an obscenity that polite company would not say

explanation.surface: Strong feelings that cannot be politely put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a term with four characters, and idiomatically a swear word unfit for polite speech.

clue.text: Woozy sage drunk from the works outing

indicators.note: a drunk is reeling and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy wise man staggering home from the office jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges WOOZY SAGE; the answer is an old word for the annual summer outing or feast of a printing works.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally the printers' annual holiday dinner and excursion, given by the employer for the staff of a print shop.

clue.text: Detailed quality of art appreciation

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the word for quality loses its tail letter

parts.note: a virtue is a good quality

explanation.surface: Fine detail as the hallmark of good art criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as de-tailed, cutting the last letter from VIRTUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word denotes a love of, or taste for, fine objects and curios, a connoisseur's knowledge of art.

clue.text: Become railway shareholder for a tanner?

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
a shareholder is a part owner of a company

explanation.surface: Someone buys shares in the railway to raise a sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence, but here it is anything that tans, i.e. makes skin darker in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tans makes one darker, so the question mark flags a whimsical word for a bronzing agent.

clue.text: Gold medal winner loses his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word for winner is dropped

parts.note: a laureate is a prize or medal winner, as in Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: An Olympic champion is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means golden, from the Latin for gold.

clue.text: View Pope Gregory thought heavenly

definitions.meaning: a point of view or slant
Gregory the Great, seeing fair English slaves in Rome

explanation.surface: A papal opinion of what is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slant is a view; and Gregory's pun made the Germanic tribesmen angelic.

clue.text: For study of people's origins, proper name must be put in

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is to be placed inside the word for proper

parts.note: proper in the sense of morally right

explanation.surface: Correct procedure for genealogy requires a name to be entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to races and peoples, the field of ethnology which studies their origins.

clue.text: Put off home — sell

parts.note: in means at home
to dispose of goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Discouraged from selling the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To make unwilling or disinclined, i.e. to deter.

clue.text: Kipling's old man was a bounder

definitions.meaning: the Just So Stories include The Sing-Song of Old Man ...
literally one that bounds or leaps, and also a cad

explanation.surface: Kipling's father was a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is something that bounds along.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling named his leaping Australian marsupial Old Man in a Just So story, and the animal travels by hops.

clue.text: Put casual shirt in bag — quite a small container

indicators.note: the words for put and the shirt go inside the word for bag

parts.note: a case is a bag for carrying things
to put is to set down
T as in T-shirt, a casual top

explanation.surface: Stuffing a T-shirt into a holdall that turns out rather small.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cartridge is a small box or enclosed case holding audio tape.

clue.text: Stuck for a reason

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Trapped for some cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run onto the shore or seabed is stranded and stuck.

clue.text: Drug giving Macbeth hallucination, some may say

indicators.note: signals that the word is pronounced like another, as some speakers say it

parts.note: Macbeth sees a dagger before him that is not there

explanation.surface: A narcotic causing Macbeth's visions, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's 'Is this a dagger which I see before me?' supplies the weapon; in non-rhotic speech it matches the South African word for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is South African for cannabis, a narcotic plant.

clue.text: So-called painter finds money abroad

indicators.note: so-called means named by its sound, the word as spoken

parts.note: a gilder applies gold leaf, a kind of decorative painter

explanation.surface: An alleged artist comes across foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Dutch currency unit, a foreign coin.

clue.text: Sounds hush-hush, this missile

indicators.note: signals the answer is said like the phrase that follows

parts.note: hush, silent, dumb, said twice

explanation.surface: A secret weapon whose noise gives it away.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanding soft-nosed bullet, a projectile fired from a gun.

clue.text: Rebel, perhaps, breaks up ancient community with force

indicators.note: the ancient city is split apart so another word can be placed inside it

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city
to prise is to force open with leverage

explanation.surface: A revolutionary uses force to break apart an old settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISE breaks UR in two; 'perhaps' warns that a rebel is just one kind of person who rises up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rises in revolt against authority, an insurgent, of whom a rebel is an example.

clue.text: African tribe has no characters that misbehave

indicators.note: letters that misbehave run wild and fall out of order

explanation.surface: An African people that has no unruly members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehave' rearranges the letters of HAS NO; the people live mainly in Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bantu people of Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

clue.text: Resulting in one's going to court

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, read as I plus S
suing means taking legal action in court

explanation.surface: The upshot is that someone takes a case to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow out or come forth as a consequence, as in a result emerging from a cause.

clue.text: Forbidding old Portuguese border

parts.note: forbidding in the sense of stern and grim

explanation.surface: A grim old frontier of Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' is an adjective (grim), not a verb; the river forms part of the border between Portugal and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This Iberian river runs along part of the boundary between Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Unfilled requisition means gaps in the files

definitions.meaning: a request for goods that is still outstanding
a military formation with wide spacing between ranks or files of soldiers

explanation.surface: An outstanding request shows holes in the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a purchase request not yet fulfilled, and a drill formation in which troops stand well spaced apart.

clue.text: Working lad cares about Warwickshire, say

indicators.note: the word for cares goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: minds in the sense of cares or is bothered

indicators.note: working in the sense of being worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy young man cares for a county in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' is the anagram signal on the next word, and 'about' the container signal. Warwickshire is a county in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwickshire is one example of the counties making up central England.

clue.text: Curious person that's laid back in word-game

indicators.note: game in the sense of a lame or crooked limb, so the letters are twisted out of shape
laid back means turned around so the abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A strange character who is very relaxed while playing a word game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' turns IE (that's) into EI; 'game' then shuffles WORD with EI.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd or eccentric individual is a strange type of person.
